issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, slipping, the car refusing to shift into top gear, or the transmission suddenly locking up or quitting.
issues.why: The electronically controlled automatic in these big Chrysler sedans is the most commonly reported expensive failure, usually after 80,000 miles or so. Worn clutches, low or burnt fluid and solenoid faults are typical causes.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition (it should be red, not brown or burnt-smelling) and use only the Chrysler-specified ATF+4. If it slips or goes into limp mode, have the codes read before it gets worse.

issues.t: Inner tie rod or steering rack failure
issues.sym: Clunking when turning, loose or wandering steering that needs constant correction, or in bad cases a sudden loss of steering control.
issues.why: Owners report inner tie rods wearing out early, tie rods separating from the rack, rack bushings breaking down and rack mounting bolts shearing. It is the most common complaint filed with NHTSA for every LHS year.
issues.next: Treat any new clunk or play in the steering as urgent. Have the tie rods, rack bushings and mounting bolts inspected and replace worn parts before driving at speed.

issues.t: Power steering leaks or heavy steering
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially on slow left turns, often with a whine or fluid spots under the front of the car.
issues.why: The power steering rack or pump leaks fluid or loses assist as it wears.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. If it keeps dropping or the steering is heavy, have the rack and pump checked for leaks. Don't keep driving with no assist.

issues.t: Fuel rail or O-ring fuel leak (recall)
issues.sym: Strong gasoline smell under the hood or in the cabin, wet fuel around the top of the engine, or in the worst case smoke or fire.
issues.why: The plastic fuel injection rail on the 3.5L V6 could develop hairline cracks and its sealing O-rings could leak, dripping fuel near hot engine parts. Chrysler recalled these cars, but owners report some leaks returning after the repair.
issues.next: Stop driving if you smell raw fuel. Have a dealer check whether recall 98V184000 was done; if it was and the leak is back, have the fuel rail and injector O-rings inspected right away.

issues.t: Car can roll away after the key is removed (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter can be moved out of Park with the key out, or the key can come out when the shifter isn't fully in Park. Owners reported the car rolling and hitting things.
issues.why: The ignition-park interlock in the floor shifter could fail. Chrysler recalled these cars to add a stronger push rod in the shifter.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Ask a Chrysler dealer to check that recall 04V021000 was completed; the repair is free.

issues.t: Front seat back can suddenly recline (recall)
issues.sym: The driver or passenger seat back suddenly drops backward, sometimes while driving.
issues.why: The bolt in the seat-back recliner mechanism could break. Chrysler recalled the cars to replace the recliner bolts.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recall 03V035000 was done. If your seat back feels loose or moves, don't drive until it is fixed.

issues.t: Shoulder belt height adjuster bolt may not hold (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The problem would only show up in a crash.
issues.why: The top mounting bolt for the adjustable shoulder belt anchor was not made correctly and may not hold in some crashes. Dealers replace the bolts.
issues.next: Ask a Chrysler dealer to check that recall 00V034000 was done.

issues.t: Front seat belt retractor may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat belt may not lock up properly when it should, or the belt is hard to pull or retract.
issues.why: Some front retractors had a molding flaw or did not meet the federal seat belt standard, so they might not restrain someone properly in a crash. Dealers replace the retractor.
issues.next: Have a dealer check whether recall 00V033000 (2000) or 01V119000 (1999) applies to your car and was completed.

issues.t: Missing B-pillar head-impact padding (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. Cars without a sunroof lacked enough head-impact protection at the pillar behind the front doors.
issues.why: These cars did not meet the federal standard for interior head impacts at the B-pillar. Chrysler supplied a padded storage bin accessory that mounts to the pillar.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether recall 01V273000 applies and have the pillar accessory installed if it is missing.

issues.t: Water pump failure damages the timing belt
issues.sym: Coolant leaks or overheating, and in some cases the engine suddenly stops and won't restart because the timing belt failed.
issues.why: On the 3.5L V6 the water pump is driven by the timing belt. A leaking or seized pump can ruin the belt, and because this is an interference engine, a snapped belt can bend valves.
issues.next: Replace the water pump whenever the timing belt is done, and follow the timing belt interval. If you see coolant leaking from behind the timing cover, get it checked before driving far.

issues.t: Overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, especially in traffic, and the car may boil over.
issues.why: Overheating is the single most-reported 1996 LHS problem. Owners trace it to failed cooling fans, cracked radiators and leaking water pumps.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if the gauge goes into the red. Have the fans, radiator, cap and water pump checked before the head gaskets are damaged.

issues.t: Oil pump failure and engine damage
issues.sym: The oil pressure light comes on, followed by knocking or ticking, and the engine can be ruined.
issues.why: Owners of 1999 cars report the oil pump failing, starving the engine of oil. It is one of the costliest problems listed for this model, averaging about 96,000 miles.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, stop the engine right away and check the oil level. Have the oil pressure tested with a gauge before driving it again.

issues.t: Stalling while driving or at idle
issues.sym: The engine dies at a stop or at highway speed, sometimes restarting right away and sometimes not. Some owners also report idle surging.
issues.why: Stalling is reported across every LHS year. The causes vary, so the fault codes stored at the time of the stall are the best clue.
issues.next: Have the codes read as soon as possible after a stall, while they are still stored. Avoid highway driving until it is diagnosed.

issues.t: Clockspring failure: airbag light, horn and cruise stop working
issues.sym: The airbag light comes on and stays on, and the horn, cruise control or steering-wheel buttons stop working.
issues.why: The clockspring, a coiled ribbon cable behind the steering wheel, breaks with wear. When it fails, the driver airbag may not deploy.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. Replacing the clockspring usually fixes it, and it restores the horn and cruise.

issues.t: Dashboard cracks over the passenger airbag
issues.sym: Cracks appear on top of the dash near the passenger airbag door and grow longer over time.
issues.why: The dash material on these years cracks with heat and age, often along the airbag door seam. Owners worry it could affect how the airbag opens.
issues.next: A dash cover hides the crack, but make sure nothing blocks the airbag door. If the airbag light is on, have it checked.

issues.t: Hood trim molding flies off at highway speed
issues.sym: A rattle or flapping from the front of the hood, then the trim piece lifts and can blow off onto the windshield or road.
issues.why: The trim molding at the front of the hood is held on with adhesive that lets go over time. Many owners report it coming off at 35 to 70 mph.
issues.next: If the molding is loose, remove it or have it reattached before your next highway trip.

issues.t: Slow tire leaks from corroded chrome wheels
issues.sym: One or more tires keep losing air slowly, even with no nail in the tread.
issues.why: The chrome plating on the factory wheels flakes and the metal underneath corrodes where the tire bead seals, and at the valve stem, letting air seep out.
issues.next: Have a tire shop clean the bead seat and apply bead sealer, or refinish or replace the wheels.

issues.t: Cloudy, yellowed headlight lenses
issues.sym: Headlights look hazy or yellow and light up the road poorly at night.
issues.why: The plastic headlight lenses on these cars break down from sunlight and age.
issues.next: Polishing or a restoration kit helps for a while. Replacement headlight assemblies are the long-term fix.

issues.t: Battery drain and interior lights cycling on their own
issues.sym: The battery goes dead every few months, and interior or dome lights turn on and off by themselves.
issues.why: Owners report an electrical drain on these cars tied to body electronics and wiring faults that keep circuits awake.
issues.next: Have a shop do a parasitic draw test to find which circuit is draining the battery.

issues.t: Worn subframe and control arm bushings
issues.sym: Clunks over bumps, front-end shake, vibration, or the car pulling to one side.
issues.why: The rubber bushings that mount the front subframe (cradle) and control arms wear out and crack.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replacing the worn bushings restores a quiet ride and steady handling.

issues.t: Lower ball joint wear
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from the front end over bumps and loose steering. A badly worn joint can separate.
issues.why: The lower ball joints wear out on these cars, and owners reported failures that affected steering.
issues.next: Have the ball joints checked for play at every tire rotation or brake job, and replace them if any looseness is found.

issues.t: Warped front brake rotors
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses and the steering wheel shakes when stopping, often at low mileage.
issues.why: The front rotors on these heavy sedans warp and wear quickly.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Replace them with quality rotors and pads, and have the lug nuts torqued correctly.

issues.t: Power window stops working
issues.sym: A window goes down and won't come back up, moves slowly, or comes off its track.
issues.why: The window regulators and motors fail on these years. Power windows are among the most-reported 1999 LHS problems.
issues.next: Have the door panel removed to check the motor and regulator. Tape or cover the window if it won't close.

issues.t: Power door locks fail or doors won't open from inside
issues.sym: Doors won't lock or unlock with the switch or remote, or a door won't open from the inside handle.
issues.why: Door lock actuators and the inside release linkage wear out.
issues.next: Replace the failing door lock actuator. If a door can't be opened from the inside, fix it promptly since it can trap a passenger.

issues.t: Trunk lid or hood supports won't hold
issues.sym: The hood or trunk lid drifts down or drops suddenly.
issues.why: The gas struts that hold the hood and trunk lid open lose pressure with age.
issues.next: Replace the support struts. Don't rely on a weak strut to hold the hood up while you work.

issues.t: Heated seat overheats and burns
issues.sym: A burning smell from the seat, or a spot on the seat that gets very hot when the heater is on.
issues.why: The heating element in the seat can overheat and burn through the upholstery.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater and unplug it if you smell burning. Have the heating element replaced.

issues.t: Gasoline smell in the cabin
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell inside the car, often at startup.
issues.why: Owners report degraded fuel vent hoses and other leaks in the fuel system. The source can be hard to find.
issues.next: A fuel smell is never normal. Have the fuel lines, vent hoses and injectors inspected for leaks.

issues.t: Instrument cluster or dash lights cut out
issues.sym: Gauges or dash lights drop out while driving and then come back.
issues.why: Owners trace this to loose ground connections and wiring faults behind the dash.
issues.next: Have the cluster grounds and connectors checked and cleaned.
